input.goal: Cut median first-response time for Tier 1 support tickets from 4.2 hours to under 2 hours by the end of Q1, without hiring more than one person.

plan.summary: Reduce median Tier 1 support first-response time from 4.2 hours to under 2 hours within 12 weeks by optimising workflows, deploying automation/tooling, and using data-driven triage — without exceeding one net-new hire.

subGoals.title: Baseline Diagnostic & Root-Cause Analysis
subGoals.description: Audit the full Tier 1 ticket lifecycle: measure where time is lost (queue wait, routing errors, missing agent context, shift gaps), segment by ticket category, volume, and time-of-day. Produce a prioritised list of the top bottlenecks driving the 4.2-hour median.

subGoals.title: Triage & Routing Optimisation
subGoals.description: Redesign ticket classification and routing rules in the support platform (e.g. Zendesk/Freshdesk) to eliminate manual re-routing. Implement keyword/tag-based auto-assignment to the right agent or queue, and set SLA breach alerts at the 90-minute mark. Target: zero tickets sitting unrouted for >15 minutes.

subGoals.title: Self-Service & Macro Automation
subGoals.description: Build and deploy a response-macro library for the top 10 ticket types (covering ~60% of volume), an interactive FAQ / chatbot deflection layer for common queries, and canned-response templates. Engineers integrate the chatbot widget into the customer-facing portal. Target: deflect 20-25% of inbound volume before it becomes a live ticket.

subGoals.title: Agent Enablement & Shift Coverage Redesign
subGoals.description: Restructure support agent shifts to match inbound volume peaks identified in the diagnostic. Create a 'first-responder' rotation role so one agent is always exclusively dedicated to new-ticket acknowledgement. Deliver a 2-hour onboarding session on new macros and tooling. Adjust staffing calendar by week 6.

subGoals.title: Real-Time Performance Dashboard
subGoals.description: Build a live operations dashboard (e.g. in Metabase or Looker) tracking median first-response time, queue depth, per-agent throughput, and SLA breach rate — updated every 15 minutes. Enables the team lead to intervene before a breach occurs and gives leadership transparent Q1 progress tracking.

subGoals.title: Steady-State Validation & Handoff
subGoals.description: Run a 2-week live monitoring period to confirm the <2-hour median is sustained, not a temporary spike. Fine-tune automation rules and shift patterns based on observed data. Document all new processes and hand off ownership to the Support Team Lead. Declare goal achieved if median holds below 2 hours for 10 consecutive business days.

roles.rationale: Core delivery resource. 70% capacity preserves bandwidth for live ticket handling while 30% is allocated to shift redesign, macro authoring, and new tooling adoption. One agent rotates as dedicated first-responder at any given time.

One engineer leads chatbot/automation integration into the customer portal and routing-rule configuration in the support platform. The second supports dashboard data pipeline and any API work needed for ticket-system automation. 60% capacity leaves headroom for existing product commitments.

Coordinates cross-functional workstreams, owns the project timeline, prioritises the automation backlog, and acts as stakeholder liaison. Low capacity allocation since this is an ops-led initiative, not a product build.
Highest-intensity role: owns the baseline diagnostic, defines the metrics framework, builds and maintains the real-time dashboard, and validates goal attainment. Central to every sub-goal.

skills: Chatbot / IVR configuration (e.g. Intercom, Ada, or native bot builder)
SQL and data pipeline development for operational metrics
REST API integration for ticket-system automation
costFactors: Fully loaded HC cost for 6 Support Agents at ~€55–70K/year = ~€27,500–35,000 for 12 weeks (70% capacity apportioned)
Fully loaded HC cost for 2 Full-Stack Engineers at ~€100–130K/year = ~€9,600–13,000 for 12 weeks (60% capacity)
Fully loaded HC cost for 1 Data Analyst at ~€80–100K/year = ~€6,100–7,700 for 12 weeks (80% capacity)
Fully loaded HC cost for 1 Product Manager at ~€90–120K/year = ~€2,000–2,700 for 12 weeks (30% capacity)
Optional: 1 new hire (Support Agent or Automation Specialist) at ~€65–85K/year fully loaded = ~€16,000–21,000 annualised if triggered
Tooling / SaaS costs: chatbot add-on or new tier ~€500–2,000 one-time or per month depending on vendor; dashboard tool licence ~€0–500/month if not already in stack

ppiLine.metric: Customer Support Cost per Ticket & SLA Penalty Exposure
ppiLine.direction: Reduce cost-per-ticket by increasing agent throughput and deflecting 20-25% of volume via automation; eliminate SLA breach penalties and reduce escalation-driven rework costs

risks.risk: Automation deflection underperforms — chatbot and macros cover fewer ticket types than projected, leaving first-response time improvement below target despite process changes.
risks.mitigation: Prioritise the macro library (low-tech, high-speed win) in weeks 3-4 before committing engineering effort to the chatbot. Set a go/no-go review at week 6 using dashboard data; if deflection <15%, redirect engineer capacity to additional routing rules and shift coverage instead.

risks.risk: Engineer capacity is consumed by competing product sprint commitments, delaying portal integration and dashboard build.
risks.mitigation: PM secures a formal 60% capacity ring-fence from the engineering manager before week 1. Scope the chatbot integration as a lightweight embed (iframe or SDK snippet) rather than a custom build to reduce engineering hours. Dashboard can be built by the Data Analyst alone if necessary.

risks.risk: Support agent resistance to shift pattern changes causes adoption delays or attrition risk.
risks.mitigation: Involve at least two senior agents in the shift redesign workshop (sub-goal 4) to co-create the schedule. Frame the first-responder rotation as a defined, time-boxed role with clear handoff, not an indefinite burden. Escalate unresolved objections to the Support Team Lead by week 5.

risks.risk: Metric is hit in the short term but regresses after Q1 due to volume growth or agent turnover.
risks.mitigation: Bake the real-time dashboard into the weekly ops review cadence permanently. Document all automation rules and routing logic so any new agent can be onboarded within one day. Set a Q2 review trigger: if median breaches 2.5 hours for 3 consecutive days, the defined escalation playbook activates automatically.

hiringNeeded.reason: The existing 6 support agents are needed at 70% capacity to maintain live ticket SLAs during the transition. Configuring and maintaining chatbot flows, macro libraries, and routing rules requires dedicated bandwidth that the current team cannot absorb without risking regression on response times mid-project. This is the one permitted hire and can double as a permanent automation owner post-Q1.
